questions.question: ________ is known as the cultivation of trees and shrubs.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Arboriculture.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Arboriculture** is the cultivation of trees and shrubs, which involves** planting, caring, and maintaining trees** and shrubs for various purposes such as landscaping, timber production, and conservation.
 
• **Arborists** are professionals who specialize in **arboriculture **and provide services such as** tree pruning, removal, and planting,** as well as diagnosing and treating** tree diseases and pests.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Viticulture **is the** cultivation of grapes** for wine production, and it involves planting and caring for grapevines, harvesting grapes, and making wine.
 
• **Aviculture **is the** breeding and raising of birds**, usually for pets or for commercial purposes such as egg or meat production.
 
• **Apiculture** is the **farming of bees for honey production, pollination**, and other bee products such as beeswax and royal jelly.

questions.question: How many total medals were won by India at Tokyo Olympics 2020 (played in 2021)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Seven.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• India won a total of **seven medals** at Tokyo Olympics 2020 (played in 2021).
 
• India won **one gold medal, two silver medals, and four bronze medals.**
 
• This is India's best performance at any Olympics so far, surpassing the previous record of six medals won at the **2012 London Olympics.**
 
• The** gold medal** was won by **Neeraj Chopra **in the** men's javelin throw event, **while the silver medals were won by **Mirabai Chanu** in weightlifting and **Ravi Kumar Dahiya** in wrestling.
 
• The four bronze medals were won by** Lovlina Borgohain** in boxing, **PV Sindhu **in badminton, **Bajrang Punia** in wrestling, and the men's hockey team. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• India won** eight medals **at Tokyo Olympics 2020, but only seven of them were won by Indian athletes.
 
• The eighth medal was won by the Indian mixed team in shooting, which included one **Indian athlete and one Croatian athlete. **

questions.question: Festival of "Ugadi" is celebrated every year on the first day of the Hindu month ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chaitra.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ugadi** is a major festival celebrated in the **southern states **of India, especially in** Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, and Karnataka.**
 
• It marks the beginning of the** Hindu lunar calendar** and is celebrated on the **first day of the month of Chaitra,** which usually falls in **March or April.**
 
• The festival is also known as **Yugadi, **which means** 'the beginning of a new age.'**
 
• It symbolizes the **start of a new year** and the **onset of spring.**
 
• On this day, people clean and decorate their **homes, wear new clothes, prepare special dishes, **and offer prayers to the gods.
 
• They also exchange **greetings and gifts** with friends and family.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Asadha** is the **fourth month** of the Hindu calendar, which usually falls in** June or July.**

 
 
• It is associated with the **monsoon season** and the onset of rains.
 
 
 
• **Jyaistha** is the** third month** of the Hindu calendar, which usually falls in **May or June**.
 
 
• It is associated with the **summer season** and the harvest of crops.
 
 
 
• **Kartika** is the **eighth month** of the Hindu calendar, which usually falls in** October or November.**
 
 
• It is associated with the **onset of winter **and the festival of Diwali.

questions.question: The technique of watering plants by making use of narrow tubes which deliver water directly at the base of the plant is called ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**drip irrigation.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Drip irrigation **is a technique where water is delivered directly to the **root zone of plants** through a network of** tubes or pipes** with small holes or emitters.
 
• This method is highly efficient as it r**educes water loss** due to evaporation, runoff, or deep percolation.
 
• Drip irrigation also helps in** reducing weed growth, soil erosion, and disease incidence.**
 
• This technique can be used for various crops, including **vegetables, fruits, flowers, and trees.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sprinkler irrigation** is a method where water is distributed through **sprinklers** that spray water over the crops.

 
 
• This method is suitable for** larger areas,** but it can lead to** water wastage **due to wind drift and evaporation. 
 
 
 
• **Canal irrigation** is a traditional method where water is supplied to crops through** canals or ditches**.
 
 
• This method is suitable for areas with **abundant water resources**, but it can lead to **waterlogging and soil salinization.**
 
 
 
• **Surface irrigation** is a method where water is applied to the soil surface and allowed to **infiltrate into the root zone.**
 
 
• This method is suitable for crops that can** tolerate wet conditions, **but it can lead to **uneven distribution of water** and nutrient leaching.

questions.question: Water comes out of the leaves in the form of vapour by a process called _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**transpiration.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Water comes out of the leaves in the form of vapour by a process called** transpiration.**
 
• Transpiration is the process of **water movement through a plant** and its** evaporation from aerial parts, **mainly from the leaves but also from stems and flowers.
 
• During transpiration, water is pulled up from the roots through the** xylem vessels** by the process of **cohesion-tension, **which creates a **negative pressure gradient.**
 
• As water molecules evaporate from the **stomata (pores)** of the leaves, they create a suction force that helps to pull more water up from the roots, maintaining the **water flow.**
 
• Transpiration serves several functions for plants, including **cooling the leaves, providing water and nutrients to the cells,** and facilitating the **uptake of minerals from the soil.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Creepers:**

 
 
• Creepers are plants that **grow horizontally along the ground **or other surfaces, using specialized structures called adventitious roots to anchor themselves.
 
• Creepers** do not** have a direct role in water movement or transpiration.
 
 
 
• **Transportation:**
 
 
• In the context of plants, transportation can refer to the** movement of water, nutrients, and other substances **through the xylem and phloem tissues, but it is not specific to transpiration.
 
 
 
• **Venation:**
 
 
• Venation refers to the **pattern of veins or vascular tissues** in plant leaves, which can be either parallel or net-like.
 
• Venation is important for** plant growth and function, **but it is not directly related to transpiration.

questions.question: Motilal Nehru, C.R. Das gave up their legal practices during which Movement?
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Non-Cooperation Movement:-**

 
 
• It was launched by **Mahatma Gandhi in 1920** as a response to the Jallianwala Bagh Massacre and the Rowlatt Act.
 
• The movement aimed to** boycott British goods, institutions, and courts **and to promote **Indian self-rule**.
 
• Motilal Nehru and C.R. Das were prominent leaders of the** Indian National Congress** who actively participated in the Non-Cooperation Movement.
 
• They gave up their** legal practices **as a symbolic gesture of their **commitment to the movement **and their rejection of British colonial rule.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Self-Respect Movement:-**

 
 
• It was a **social reform movement **in South India led by **E.V. Ramasamy (Periyar)** in the 1920s and 1930s.
 
• It aimed to promote the **rights and dignity of non-Brahmin castes **and to challenge Brahmin hegemony.
 
 
 
• **Quit India Movement:-**
 
 
• It was a mass civil disobedience movement launched by **Mahatma Gandhi in 1942** demanding immediate** British withdrawal **from India.
 
 
 
• **Civil Disobedience Movement:-**
 
 
• It​ was a campaign of **nonviolent civil disobedience** led by Mahatma Gandhi in **1930 **to challenge British colonial rule and to demand Indian independence.
 
• It included the** Salt Satyagraha**, in which Indians defied British salt laws by making** their own salt.**

questions.question: Rainfall is measured by an instrument called the ________.
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Rain Gauge:-**

 
 
• The instrument used to measure rainfall is called a** rain gauge.**
 
• It is a simple tool that consists of a **cylindrical container **with a funnel on the top and a measuring scale on the side.
 
• The rain gauge **collects rainwater,** and the amount of water collected is measured using the scale.
 
• Rain gauges are commonly used by** meteorologists, hydrologists, and farmers** to monitor rainfall and plan for irrigation.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• It is a device that **collects rainwater for later use.**
 
• Rainwater harvesting is a sustainable way to conserve water and reduce your reliance on municipal water supplies. 
 
 
 
• **Rain Calculator:-**
 
 
• It is a tool that can be **used to calculate the amount of rainfall that is expected to fall in a given area.**
 
• This can be useful for a variety of purposes, such as planning irrigation schedules, preventing flooding, and estimating the amount of water that can be collected for rainwater harvesting.
 
 
 
• **Precipitator:-**
 
 
• It is a device that **removes particulate matter from a gas stream.**
 
• It is used in a variety of industries, including power generation, cement production, and metal processing.

questions.question: Which force is responsible for deflecting winds towards the right and left in northern and southern Hemisphere respectively?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Coriolis force.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Coriolis force:-**

 
 
• It​ is responsible for **deflecting winds** towards the** right and left** in the northern and southern hemispheres respectively.
 
• This force is a result of the** rotation of the Earth** and the** inertia of the moving air masses.**
 
• The Coriolis force is** strongest at the poles **and **weakest at the equator.**
 
• This force also affects **ocean currents** and the movement of objects such as **airplanes and missiles.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Magnetic force:**

 
 
• This force is caused by the **interaction of charged particles **with **Earth's magnetic field.**
 
• It can affect the behavior of **charged particles** in the atmosphere, but it does not have a significant impact on wind deflection.
 
 
 
• **Gravitational force:**
 
 
• This force is responsible for** keeping objects on Earth's surface** and is not directly related to wind deflection.
 
 
 
• **Frictional force:**
 
 
• This force is caused by the interaction of air with the Earth's surface and can affect **wind speed and direction**, but it is not responsible for wind deflection.

questions.question: The Deccan Riots of 1875 took place in ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Maharashtra.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Deccan Riots of 1875** were a series of riots that took place in the **Deccan region of British India.**
 
• The riots were sparked by** economic grievances** among the** local peasantry,** who were suffering from** high taxes and low crop yields.**
 
• The riots were particularly intense in the districts of **Poona and Satara i**n present-day Maharashtra.
 
• The British colonial government responded to the riots with a **heavy hand, using military force** to suppress the rebellion and arresting many of the leaders.
 
• The **Deccan Riots** were part of a larger wave of **peasant unrest** that swept across India in the late 19th century, as rural communities struggled to cope with the **demands of colonial rule **and **capitalist agriculture.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• The region was then part of the **British province of Punjab.**

questions.question: The materials through which objects can be seen, but not clearly are known as ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** translucent materials.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Translucent materials** allow light to pass through them, but they **scatter the light,** making objects **appear blurry or hazy.**
 
• Examples of translucent materials include** frosted glass, wax paper, and some plastics**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Conducting materials,** such as metals, allow **electricity **to flow through them easily.
 
• **Transparent materials,** such as clear glass or plastic, allow light to pass through them **without scattering,** making objects appear clear and sharp.
 
• **Opaque materials,** such as **wood or metal**, do not allow light to pass through them at all.

questions.question: "Gopuram" or temple entrance is a feature of which temple architecture?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**South Indian temple architecture.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gopuram** is a prominent feature of **South Indian temple architecture**, which is known for its towering gateways with **intricate carvings and sculptures.**
 
• These gateways usually lead to the **main sanctum **of the temple and are considered as a symbol of the **temple's grandeur and spiritual significance.**
 
• **Buddhist architecture**, on the other hand, is characterized by** stupa or pagoda structures** that usually contain **relics or sacred objects.**
 
• **Jain architecture** is known for its **intricate marble carvings** and use of **vibrant colors**, but it does not feature gopurams.
 
• **North Indian temple architecture**, also known as Nagara style, is characterized by its** shikhara or spire structures**, but again, it does not feature gopurams.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Buddhist architecture is commonly found in countries like** India, Nepal, Sri Lanka, China, Japan, and Thailand.**
 
• Jain architecture is mostly found in western India, particularly in the **state of Rajasthan.**
 
• North Indian temple architecture is prominent in states like** Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, and Rajasthan.**
